original_test_intent: Read the BMC thermal sensor inventory and state through Redfish and verify the specified sensor descriptions and agreed attributes match the platform specification.
original_method: Discover the target Chassis Thermal resource, validate each temperature sensor's identity and schema, and compare static descriptors plus only explicitly governed readings, units, status and thresholds against a versioned oracle without thermal stimulation.
manual_activity: Provide the firmware-matched Chassis/Thermal schema, expected sensor population and descriptor matrix, plus rules for units, unavailable/stale readings, thresholds and any permitted dynamic-value tolerance.
required_inputs: Expected sensor identity and description matrix
safety_requirements: No hardcoded credentials or TLS bypass
Do not write fan control, thresholds, power limits, trip points or thermal policy
Do not inject a thermal fault or create load
Bind readings to stable sensor identity and units
Fail closed on stale, unavailable, duplicated or wrong-chassis data
agent_execution_scope: Use secret-backed read-only access over verified TLS
Evaluate availability, units, health and threshold applicability
Report dynamic values without inventing limits
engineer_actions: Approve field scope, units and dynamic-reading policy
Confirm no thermal stimulus is part of this case

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: It reads a relevant array, but hardcodes the ChassisId, bypasses TLS, drops resource context and supplies neither sensor identity nor the specification and dynamic-reading rules needed by the criterion.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Follow the advertised Thermal link, securely retain the complete resource, validate every required temperature sensor and compare static descriptions plus explicitly approved status/reading fields with the versioned sensor oracle.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Thermal Sensor read-only scope and 15/10 timing remain; ChassisId, sensor list, thresholds, tolerances and stale-data semantics are not inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use identity-aware schema validation and a two-part comparison: deterministic static descriptors, then separately governed dynamic telemetry with timestamp, units and availability checks.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces the placeholder and unqualified YES with resource discovery, an external sensor oracle and explicit dynamic-data semantics while preserving all diagnostics.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Validates Redfish-reported sensor inventory and state only; it does not validate sensor accuracy against calibrated equipment, threshold trip behavior, fan response or thermal protection.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Readings naturally vary with ambient and workload, and stale or unavailable values can look numerically plausible unless timestamps, status and sensor identity are checked.

project_override_considerations: If this firmware exposes Sensor resources instead of or alongside legacy Chassis Thermal arrays, use the project-approved mapping and preserve both identity paths in evidence. Do not treat a matching numeric reading as proof of the named sensor description.
expected_evidence: HTTP status and complete response hash
Stable per-sensor identity, description, reading, units and status
Static and dynamic comparison results separated
No thermal stimulus or control write

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, generic read-only Procedure and specification-match Criteria consistently indicate a Thermal Sensor inspection. The missing endpoint and oracle are incompleteness rather than contradictory intent.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The sensor schema, identity matrix and dynamic-reading policy are definable package inputs, so the case is REQUIRES rather than irreducibly BLOCKED.

review_improvement: Turns an unauditable array dump into a sensor-identity-aware comparison that cannot confuse changing telemetry with static description compliance or silently introduce thermal stress.
independent_technical_reasoning: Thermal resources mix static identity, units and threshold metadata with readings that depend on time, ambient conditions and workload. A specification match therefore needs deterministic comparison for names and supported fields while live values require an explicitly supplied tolerance or health policy. Missing, duplicated, stale or unavailable sensors must be reported distinctly from numeric mismatch. The source authorizes only inspection, so fan writes, threshold changes and heat/load stimulus would be scope expansion even if they are useful in a different thermal test.
